en: The Questions of King Milinda,
Chapter on Investigation 7:
The Question on Eye-consciousness and the Other [Sense-Consciousnesses]
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, where visual consciousness arises, does mental consciousness also arise there?
"Yes, Great King, where visual consciousness arises, mental consciousness also arises there."
“Venerable Nāgasena, does visual consciousness arise first and mental consciousness later, or does mental consciousness arise first and visual consciousness later?
“Great King, visual consciousness arises first, and mental consciousness arises later.
“But venerable Nāgasena, does visual consciousness command mental consciousness, saying: ‘Wherever I arise...”
“Or does the mind-consciousness command the eye-consciousness, saying:
‘Wherever you shall arise, there I too shall arise’?
“Certainly not, Great King; there is no conversation between them one with another.”
“Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that where visual consciousness arises, there mental consciousness also arises?
“Because of its slope, O Great King, because of its being a door, because of habit, and because of its habitual operation.
“Venerable Nāgasena, how is it by way of its slope that where visual consciousness arises, there mental consciousness also arises?”
“Make a simile.
“What do you think, Great King, when the rain falls from the sky, by what way would the water go?
“Venerable sir, it would go by the way that is low-lying.”
“Then at another time, if it were to rain, by which way would that water go?
“Venerable sir, it would go by the same way as the previous water went.
“But what, great king, does the previous water command the subsequent water: ‘By the way that I go, you too must go’?”
“You too should go by that [path],” or he directs the later water toward the earlier water, saying, “Where you will go, there I too shall go.
“Certainly not, venerable sir; they do not converse with one another, but they flow because of their downward slope.”
“In the same way, Great King, because of its downward slope, wherever eye-consciousness arises, there mind-consciousness also arises.
Yet eye-consciousness does not command mind-consciousness, saying, ‘Wherever I arise, you too must arise there’;
nor does mind-consciousness command eye-consciousness, saying, ‘Wherever you will arise, [I shall arise there].’”
‘I too shall arise there,’ yet there is no conversation between them with one another, for they arise due to their inclination.
“Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that where eye-consciousness arises because of the door, there mental consciousness also arises?
Give me a simile.”
“What do you think, great king? Suppose a king had a frontier city with strong ramparts and gate-towers, and a single gate; if a man there wished to go out, by what way would he go out?
“By the gate, venerable sir, he would go out.
“Then suppose another man wished to go out, by what way would he go out?”
“Venerable sir, the first man who went out would go out by that same way.

“But what do you think, Great King? Does the first man command the last man, saying, ‘Go by the way that I am going,’ or does the last man command the first man, saying, ‘Go by the way that you will go’?”
“I too shall go by that way.
“No indeed, venerable sir; there is no conversation between them, for they are going because of the door.
“In the same way, great king, because of the door, wherever eye-consciousness arises, there mental consciousness also [arises].”
Eye-consciousness does not command mind-consciousness, saying, "Wherever I arise, you too must arise there";
nor does mind-consciousness command eye-consciousness, saying, "Wherever you will arise, I too shall arise there.
There is no conversation between them one with another; they arise because they have doors [as their respective bases]."
“Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that, by virtue of habituation, wherever eye-consciousness arises, there mind-consciousness also arises?
Give me an illustration.
“What do you think, Great King? Suppose a first cart were to go; then by which way would a second cart go?”
“Venerable sir, it would go by the same path as the first cart has gone.
“But what then, great king? Does the first cart command the second cart, saying, ‘Go by the same path that I am going,’ or does the second cart command the first cart, saying, ‘You…”
“You will go; I too shall go with you.
“No indeed, venerable sir; they do not converse with one another, for they proceed because of their habitual practice.
“In the same way, great king, because of habitual practice, wherever visual consciousness arises, there mental consciousness also [arises].”

Eye-consciousness does not command mind-consciousness, saying, ‘Wherever I arise, you too should arise there,’ nor does mind-consciousness command eye-consciousness, saying, ‘Wherever you will arise, I too shall arise there.
There is no conversation between them; they arise simply through habituation.”
“Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that where eye-consciousness arises, there mental consciousness also arises because of familiarity?
Please provide an illustration.

“Just as, Great King, for one who is a beginner in the arts of finger-calculation, counting, reckoning, writing, or painting, there is slowness; but at a later time, through careful practice and familiarity, there is no longer any slowness.”
In the same way, Great King, because of habitual practice, wherever eye-consciousness arises, there mind-consciousness also arises.
Yet eye-consciousness does not command mind-consciousness, saying, "Wherever I arise, you too must arise there";
nor does mind-consciousness command eye-consciousness, saying, "Wherever you will arise..."
“I too shall arise there. There is no conversation between them with one another; they arise because of their habitual practice.
“Venerable Nāgasena, where ear-consciousness arises, does mind-consciousness also arise there?
…pe… where nose-consciousness arises … where tongue-consciousness arises … where body-consciousness arises, does mind-consciousness also arise there?”
“Yes, great king, wherever body-consciousness arises, there mind-consciousness also arises.
“But, venerable Nāgasena, does body-consciousness arise first and mind-consciousness afterwards, or does mind-consciousness arise first and body-consciousness afterwards?
“Body-consciousness, great king, arises first; mind-consciousness arises afterwards.”
“But why, venerable Nāgasena,
do they arise through mutual conversation, yet there is no conversation between them?
“You are clever, venerable Nāgasena.”
The seventh question: on eye-consciousness and so forth.
